The 1900 census entry for Christian P. Hole in Fairview Township, Polk County indexes his birth year as **1877**. The profile records his birth year as **1875**. The death index (finding 2 below) also records 1875, and both agree on Norway as birthplace.

A two-year discrepancy in a census return is the kind of variance that falls within ordinary estimation — ages were reported by whoever answered the enumerator's door and were often rounded. However, the death index, which is drawn from a registration at the time of death and tends to be more reliable for birth year, agrees with the profile's 1875. The two records disagree with each other, not just with the profile, and the death index carries the more authoritative value for birth year.

This cannot be settled from the index alone: it is either an enumerator error on the census page or a genuine two-year uncertainty. The source is good evidence for residence and household, and nothing here warrants detaching it.

Next: re-open the original census page (this collection is "database with images," so the image is available) and confirm whether the enumerator wrote 1877 or whether the age column was misread during indexing. If the page shows 1877, that is ordinary variance to note; if it shows something closer to 1875, use the index-correction path on FamilySearch to fix the indexed value. Keep the source attached either way.

**2. "Minnesota Death Index, 1908-2002" — indexing error in death year**

The death index entry for Christian P. Hole indexes his death date as **10 June 1954**. The profile records the death as **10 June 1945** — the day and month match exactly, only the year differs (1954 vs. 1945). The birth year indexed in this same record is 1875, consistent with the profile.
